title: Ease multi index and autocomplete with react-instantsearch
body:
This a preview of what I've done to ease the multi index / autocomplete use case by using react-instantsearch. 

I'd love to have your feedback of what is already done. You can play with the feature by looking at the story "Multi Index". I also updated two recipes for you to see the changes. 

While developing this feature I change some internal implementations: 
* The query is now added as a metadata. The `connectCurrentRefinement` filter them if the prop `clearsQuery` is not their. 
* The pagination reset to first page is now explicitly done by each widget that needs it
* When unmounting a widget, we clear the empty key from the `search state`. Will probably be moved to the `onSearchStateChange` function. 

What I want to do next with this branch: 

* refactor the derivation usage inside `createInstantSearchManager`. I added some basic tests to support this refactoring. @bobylito if you have any advice, pleases shoot :) 
* add a real autocomplete example without the usage of an external component. Don't know if we should go for a recipe, or do a nice demo. 
* update all the documentation => api, guide. 
 
see #1962

about the preview: it redirects `Index.html` to `index.html`, is there some way we can avoid that, maybe just by calling it `<Index>.html` for example?
I'm in the middle of the refactoring based on your comments. I believe this is due to the new name "Index".

In term of changes: 

- Reseting the pagination should be done at each connector level inside the "refine" function when returning the search state. 
- The current page now appears inside the search state when a widget is used
- Query values are part of the items prop of the connectCurrentRefinements connector. Behaviour is unchanged, query will be filtered if `clearsQuery` prop is false.
- Add the index name to all the current refinements items. (not used by our widgets yet, but available if needed).

Pending questions: 

- Should we find a way to avoid the need of a VirtualWidget when using an external autocomplete component?

Should be OK for beta release but ultimately might be not that easy
